new.title: Descend into the eight levels of Derinkuyu Underground City
new.desc: Derinkuyu is often called the deepest of Cappadocia's underground cities, carved into soft volcanic tuff beneath the town. It opened to visitors in the 1960s, and only part of it can be walked. Ventilation shafts, stables, a church and rolling stone doors are all still visible.
new.tip: Arrive at opening to beat the tour buses; passages are low and steep, so wear flat shoes. Follow the red arrows down and the blue arrows up.
new.q: Derinkuyu Yeraltı Şehri, Merkez, Derinkuyu, Nevşehir

new.title: Squeeze through the tunnels of Kaymaklı Underground City
new.desc: Kaymaklı has eight levels, of which four are open to visitors. Its tunnels are narrower and steeper than Derinkuyu's and hold kitchens, wine presses, storerooms and a rolling-stone door. It was used as a refuge by local communities for centuries.
new.tip: Go early or late to avoid crowds; allow at least an hour. Not ideal if you are claustrophobic.
new.q: Kaymaklı Yeraltı Şehri, Kaymaklı, Merkez, Nevşehir

new.title: Explore quiet Özkonak Underground City on Mt Idis
new.desc: Özkonak lies about 14 km from Avanos, on the northern slopes of Mt Idis. It has the same wine reservoirs, ventilation shafts and rolling stone doors as the bigger underground cities but is far less crowded. Parts of the complex have not been cleared.
new.tip: Weekdays are often almost empty. Combine with Gülşehir and Hacıbektaş on a northern loop.
new.q: Özkonak Yeraltı Şehri, Özkonak, Avanos, Nevşehir

new.title: See the frescoes of Karşı Kilise (St Jean) in Gülşehir
new.desc: Karşı Kilise, 'the church on the other side', is a two-level rock-cut church near Gülşehir with a lower church beneath an upper one. The barrel vault of the upper church carries painted Old Testament prophets. It is also known as the Church of St Jean.
new.tip: Entry is covered by the Museum Card. The building is small, so visit outside tour-bus hours.
new.q: Karşı Kilise (St Jean Kilisesi), Gülşehir, Nevşehir

new.title: Wander the rock-cut Açıksaray settlement near Gülşehir
new.desc: Açıksaray ('Open Palace') is a cluster of cave dwellings, chapels and halls carved into the rock about 5 km outside Gülşehir. Its original purpose is unclear, and it is far quieter than the better-known valleys. It sits just off the Nevşehir to Kırşehir road.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes for the loose ground; allow about an hour. A taxi from Gülşehir is the easiest way.
new.q: Açıksaray Kaya Yerleşimi, Açıksaray, Gülşehir, Nevşehir

new.title: Visit the Hacı Bektaş Veli Museum and Bektashi lodge
new.desc: The 13th-century saint Hacı Bektaş Veli founded the Bektashi order here, and the lodge complex with its tomb, mosque, guesthouse and kitchen is now a museum. It was restored in 1958 to 1964 and opened as an ethnography museum in 1964. Pilgrims visit all year.
new.tip: Commemorative ceremonies fill the town in mid-August. Dress modestly.
new.q: Hacıbektaş Veli Müzesi, Hacıbektaş, Nevşehir

new.title: Join the Hacı Bektaş Veli commemoration in mid-August
new.desc: Each year around 16 to 18 August, Hacıbektaş hosts commemoration events with semah dances, music and talks in honour of Hacı Bektaş Veli. Visitors from across Türkiye and abroad fill the town.
new.tip: Book accommodation well ahead in Nevşehir or Kırşehir if you plan to stay overnight.
new.q: Hacıbektaş Veli Dergahı, Hacıbektaş, Nevşehir

new.title: See the Kurşunlu Mosque complex of Damat İbrahim Paşa
new.desc: The grand vizier Nevşehirli Damat İbrahim Paşa built this külliye in Nevşehir in 1726 to 1727, the largest and oldest mosque complex in town. It includes a medrese, soup kitchen, library and fountain. The complex reflects his remaking of his home town in the 1720s.
new.tip: Free to enter outside prayer times. Pair with a lunch of testi kebabı in the town centre.
new.q: Kurşunlu Camii, Damat İbrahim Paşa Külliyesi, Nevşehir Merkez

new.title: Break open a testi kebabı at Haliçi Nevşehir Tavacı Mustafa
new.desc: Testi kebabı, meat and vegetables slow-cooked in a sealed clay pot that is cracked open at the table, is the signature dish of Nevşehir. Local food guides list Tavacı Mustafa among the places to try it in Nevşehir town.
new.tip: Ask whether the pot needs ordering in advance. Portions are generous.
new.q: Tavacı Mustafa Restaurant, Sümer Mahallesi, Yeni Sanayi 8. Blok, Nevşehir Merkez, Nevşehir

new.title: Eat Nevşehir home-style dishes at Şükrüoğulları Restoran
new.desc: Şükrüoğulları is a local restaurant in Nevşehir town named in the city's food guide among places to eat testi kebabı and regional dishes. It serves residents rather than tour groups.
new.tip: Go at lunch when the daily dishes are fresh. Confirm opening hours on the day.
new.q: Şükrüoğulları Cafe Restaurant, İstiklal Caddesi, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Finish a Nevşehir meal with Ottoman dessert at Nostalji
new.desc: Nostalji Restoran in Nevşehir is named in a local food guide for traditional Ottoman-style desserts, including the town's aside, a sweet made of flour and sugar. A good stop after a testi kebabı lunch.
new.tip: Try the aside or a seasonal dessert with Turkish tea.
new.q: Nostalji Restaurant, Kale Sokak, Gaferli Mahallesi, Göreme, Nevşehir

new.title: Have home cooking at the Old Greek House in Mustafapaşa
new.desc: The Old Greek House is an unrestored Ottoman-era Greek mansion in Mustafapaşa (Sinasos). Meals are served in the courtyard or in upstairs rooms, with home-style dishes such as köfte, güveç and hünkar beğendi.
new.tip: Reserve ahead, especially in summer. Ask for a table in the courtyard.
new.q: Old Greek House, Şahin Caddesi No:12, Davutlu, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Dine at Gorgoli in a Mustafapaşa stone house
new.desc: Gorgoli is a restaurant on Yılmaz Sokak in Mustafapaşa, listed in the Michelin Guide as a Plate restaurant. It serves Anatolian dishes in a restored stone house in the former Greek village of Sinasos.
new.tip: Book a table; it is small. Wander the Greek-era streets before or after.
new.q: Gorgoli, Yılmaz Sokak, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Sip Turkish coffee at the Kapadokya Kahve Müzesi in Mustafapaşa
new.desc: The Kapadokya Kahve Müzesi (Cappadocia Coffee Museum) is a café-museum in Mustafapaşa. It shows coffee-making tools and serves Turkish coffee, a good rest in the old Greek village.
new.tip: Ask for coffee cooked in hot sand. Check opening hours locally as they vary by season.
new.q: Kapadokya Kahve Müzesi, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: See the Ayios Konstantinos-Eleni Church in Mustafapaşa
new.desc: The church on the main square of Mustafapaşa (Sinasos) was built in 1729 and restored in 1850. Sinasos was home to a large Greek Orthodox community until the 1924 population exchange, and the mansions around the square date from that era.
new.tip: Combine with a stroll through the old stone streets; check whether it is open or ask at the square.
new.q: Aios Konstantinos Eleni Kilisesi, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Discover Tahtalı Kilise in the Soğanlı valleys
new.desc: Soğanlı has rock-cut churches, dovecotes and houses spread over two branching valleys, inhabited by Byzantine monks between the 9th and 13th centuries. Tahtalı Kilise (St Barbara) in the southern valley has some of the best-preserved decoration. Karabaş and Yılanlı churches lie in the northern branch.
new.tip: No public transport; come by car or tour. Take water and spend a half day walking both valleys.
new.q: Soğanlı Arkeolojik Sit Alanı, Soğanlı, Yeşilhisar, Kayseri

new.title: Eat home-style food in the garden of Soğanlı Kapadokya Restaurant
new.desc: A small garden restaurant in the Soğanlı valley village, praised by visitors for home-cooked dishes and friendly owners. It is one of few places to eat beside the churches.
new.tip: Prices are modest; order the day's home-style dishes. Check opening hours in winter.
new.q: Soğanlı Kapadokya Restaurant, Soğanlı, Yeşilhisar, Kayseri

new.title: Walk the Ihlara Valley from the 360 steps to Belisırma
new.desc: The Ihlara Valley is a 14 km canyon cut by the Melendiz stream, lined with more than a dozen rock-cut churches. From the visitor centre a stairway of 360 steps leads down to the river, then a shaded path runs north to Belisırma. A full walk to Selime takes 7 to 8 hours.
new.tip: Start early in summer; the Ağaçaltı to Belisırma section is the best half-day walk. A museum card is accepted at the gate.
new.q: Ihlara Vadisi Turistik Tesisleri, Ihlara, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Find the three-headed snake in Yılanlı Church, Ihlara
new.desc: Yılanlı Kilise (Snake Church) in the Ihlara Valley is known for a fresco of a three-headed snake and vivid scenes of the damned. It is one of the churches along the river path between the steps and Belisırma.
new.tip: Follow the path south from the steps. Wear shoes with grip, as steps are steep.
new.q: Yılanlı Kilise, Ihlara Vadisi, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Eat tandır kebab at Ihlara Vadisi Ağaçaltı Restaurant
new.desc: Ağaçaltı Restaurant stands by the Ihlara Valley and is known for tandır kebab, lamb slow-cooked in a clay oven. It is a convenient lunch stop beside the Church Beneath a Tree.
new.tip: Try the tandır kebab or fresh trout and sit near the stream.
new.q: Ihlara Vadisi Ağaçaltı Restaurant, Ihlara, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Eat river trout at Belisırma Restaurant over the Melendiz
new.desc: Belisırma, about 4 km north of Ihlara village, has restaurants on platforms over the Melendiz stream. Belisırma Restaurant is known for fresh trout and has an enclosed section open all year.
new.tip: Hikers finish the valley walk here. Order the trout and ask for a riverside platform.
new.q: Belisırma Restaurant, Belisırma, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Look over the valley from Belisırma Seyir Restaurant
new.desc: Belisırma Seyir Restaurant is rated well for valley views and service. It is a short climb above the village, on the route back from the churches.
new.tip: Good for a sunset tea after the hike. Budget around 400 to 600 TRY a head in recent reviews.
new.q: Belisırma Seyir Restaurant, Belisırma, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Try baked trout at Aslan Restaurant in Belisırma
new.desc: Aslan Belisırma Köyü Restaurant is a village restaurant in Belisırma known for fresh baked trout, taken from the valley's streams.
new.tip: Arrive before the tour groups, around noon; trout is the dish to order.
new.q: Aslan Restaurant, Belisırma Köyü, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Climb through Selime Cathedral, the largest rock-cut monastery
new.desc: Selime Cathedral is a two-storey rock-cut complex at the northern end of the Ihlara Valley, described as the largest cathedral in Cappadocia. Carved from a volcanic cliff, it has a long hall, kitchens and stables, and some scholars now think it was a Byzantine mansion.
new.tip: Take a torch for the dark rooms. Combine with a valley walk from Belisırma.
new.q: Selime Katedrali, Selime, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Visit Sivişli Church above Güzelyurt (Gelveri)
new.desc: Güzelyurt was Gelveri, a Greek Orthodox town until 1924, and its rock-carved houses are among the best examples of Cappadocian architecture. Sivişli Church (St Anargyros) stands on a hill opposite the Cami Kilise and is partly rock-carved, partly built of cut stone.
new.tip: Also see the Gelveri houses in town. Good with an Ihlara day trip.
new.q: Sivişli Kilisesi, Güzelyurt, Aksaray

new.title: Walk through the vast Sultanhanı Caravanserai
new.desc: Built in 1228 to 1229 under the Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Keykubad I, Sultanhanı is regarded as the largest Seljuk caravanserai in Anatolia. Its elaborate marble portal leads to an open courtyard with a central mosque and a covered hall behind.
new.tip: Fee is small; the village is on the Aksaray to Konya road. Look up the portal carving.
new.q: Sultanhanı Kervansarayı, Sultanhanı, Aksaray

new.title: Stop at the Seljuk Ağzıkarahan Caravanserai near Aksaray
new.desc: Ağzıkarahan was built between 1231 and 1239 on the Aksaray to Nevşehir stretch of the Silk Road. It is a smaller, well-preserved Seljuk inn with a carved portal and a courtyard.
new.tip: Usually a quick stop on the way between Aksaray and Cappadocia; ask at the entrance for the key-holder if closed.
new.q: Ağzıkarahan Kervansarayı, Ağzıkara, Aksaray

new.title: See the leaning Eğri Minare in Aksaray
new.desc: The Eğri Minare (Red Minaret), built in brick between about 1221 and 1236, leans markedly and has stood so for around 800 years. It is a symbol of Aksaray, next to the Ulu Cami area.
new.tip: Free to view; the old town is compact so combine with the Zinciriye Madrasa museum.
new.q: Eğri Minare, Aksaray Merkez

new.title: See the Aksaray Museum in the Zinciriye Madrasa
new.desc: The Zinciriye Madrasa was built in 1336 by Yahşi Bey in the Karamanid period and now houses the Aksaray Museum. It holds finds from Aşıklı Höyük and other Central Anatolian sites alongside the portal's stone carving.
new.tip: A quick, uncrowded stop in town; check opening days locally.
new.q: Aksaray Müzesi, Zinciriye Medresesi, Aksaray Merkez

new.title: Visit the Karamanid Ulu Cami of Aksaray
new.desc: Aksaray's Ulu Cami dates from 1408 to 1409 under the Karamanids and stands in the city centre. Its decoration is typical of the post-Seljuk beylik period.
new.tip: Free; dress modestly and avoid prayer times.
new.q: Ulu Cami, Aksaray Merkez

new.title: Climb Hasan Dağı, the 3,268 m volcano above Aksaray
new.desc: Hasan Dağı is a dormant stratovolcano reaching 3,268 m, the second-highest peak of Central Anatolia. A summit hike is a challenging full-day or two-day trek with views over the Tuz Gölü basin and Cappadocia.
new.tip: Best from June to September; take layers, water and a local guide. Snow can remain into early summer.
new.q: Hasan Dağı, Helvadere, Aksaray

new.title: Visit the Seljuk Alaaddin Mosque in Niğde castle
new.desc: Niğde's Alaaddin Mosque, founded in 1223 under Sultan Alaeddin Keykubad, stands on the castle hill. It has kept much of its original character and still serves as a mosque.
new.tip: Free; the castle grounds above the old town give views of Niğde and the Aladağlar on clear days.
new.q: Alaaddin Camii, Niğde Kalesi, Niğde Merkez

new.title: See the Gothic-style portal of Sungur Bey Mosque in Niğde
new.desc: The Sungur Bey Mosque was completed around 1335 under Ilkhanid governor Sungur Bey and has a tomb beside it. Scholars note Gothic-influenced elements in its design, and it lost its minarets after use as a gunpowder store in the 18th century.
new.tip: Free; combine with the nearby Ak Medrese and Alaaddin Mosque in an hour's walk.
new.q: Sungur Bey Camii, Niğde Merkez, Niğde

new.title: Study the Ak Medrese of 1409 in Niğde
new.desc: The Ak Medrese was built in 1409 in the Karamanid period and is among the largest historic buildings in Niğde. Its 1415 endowment deed is an important source on the city's history.
new.tip: Check whether it is open; the carved portal can be seen anyway.
new.q: Ak Medrese, Saruhan Mahallesi, Niğde Merkez, Niğde

new.title: Find the Smiling Virgin at Gümüşler Monastery
new.desc: Gümüşler Monastery is a rock-cut Byzantine monastery about 9 to 10 km from Niğde, with a courtyard carved into the hillside. Its frescoes, among them the well-known Smiling Virgin Mary, date from the 8th to 12th centuries by various estimates. It was rediscovered in 1963.
new.tip: Catch it in morning light. Entry is covered by the Museum Card; the site is small, about 45 minutes.
new.q: Gümüşler Manastırı, Gümüşler, Niğde

new.title: Hike beneath Demirkazık in the Aladağlar National Park
new.desc: Demirkazık (about 3,756 m) is a limestone peak of the Aladağlar range in the Taurus, popular with climbers and trekkers. The Demirkazık village area is the trailhead for routes into Aladağlar National Park, with alpine meadows and canyons.
new.tip: Best from late June to September; overnight stays at mountain huts need a local guide.
new.q: Demirkazık Köyü, Çamardı, Niğde

new.title: Taste forgotten Niğde recipes at Tabal Gastronomi Evi
new.desc: Tabal Gastronomi Evi is a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant in an old mansion at the foot of Niğde Castle, opposite the Ak Medrese. The menu revives local Niğde dishes, including the geographically indicated Niğde tava.
new.tip: Bor söğürmesi is made to order and is mostly a Ramadan dish, so ask in advance.
new.q: Tabal Gastronomi Evi, Ak Medrese Caddesi No:23, Saruhan Mahallesi, Niğde Merkez, Niğde

new.title: Cross the Seljuk Kesikköprü bridge and see Cacabey Han
new.desc: The Kesikköprü bridge over the Kızılırmak was built in 1248, and beside it stands the Cacabey Han, commissioned by Nureddin Caca, the Seljuk emir of Kırşehir. The caravanserai is now used as a culture house.
new.tip: It is out of town on the Kırşehir to Kaman road; a quiet picnic spot by the river.
new.q: Kesikköprü Kervansarayı (Caca Bey Hanı), Kesikköprü, Kırşehir

new.title: Visit the tomb of Ahi Evran in Kırşehir
new.desc: The Ahi Evran complex holds the tomb of Ahi Evran-ı Veli, founder of the Ahi guild brotherhood of craftsmen. The mosque and tomb date from 1482. A museum of Ahi culture sits beside the complex.
new.tip: Free; the Ahi Festival in September brings events to the city.
new.q: Ahi Evran Külliyesi, Kırşehir Merkez

new.title: See the excavation inside the Kaman-Kalehöyük Museum
new.desc: Kaman-Kalehöyük is a mound near Kaman where Japanese-led excavation since 1986 has uncovered layers from the Early Bronze Age onward. The museum is built in the shape of a mound, so visitors see finds and the dig together, and a Japanese garden is nearby.
new.tip: A little over an hour from Kırşehir; check seasonal hours.
new.q: Kaman Kalehöyük Arkeoloji Müzesi, Çağırkan, Kaman, Kırşehir

new.title: Watch flamingos on Seyfe Lake near Kırşehir
new.desc: Seyfe Gölü is a shallow salt lake about 36 km from Kırşehir, a bird reserve with a large flamingo colony and, in autumn, stopover flocks of ducks.
new.tip: Bring binoculars; flamingos are most numerous in spring to early summer.
new.q: Seyfe Gölü Kuş Cenneti, Çiçekdağı, Kırşehir

new.title: Look at the 13th-century Melikgazi Tomb in Kırşehir
new.desc: The Melikgazi Kümbeti stands in the south-east of the city centre and is thought to date from the 13th century. It is one of the older Seljuk-era funerary buildings of Kırşehir.
new.tip: Quick stop; combine with Ahi Evran and the Kırşehir museum.
new.q: Melikgazi Kümbeti, Kırşehir Merkez, Kırşehir

new.title: Walk the walls of Iron Age Kerkenes
new.desc: Kerkenes is a late Iron Age city founded by the Phrygians in the 7th century BC on Kerkenes Mountain near Sorgun. Its 7 km of stone fortifications, pierced by seven gates, enclose 2.5 sq km. The city was burned and abandoned.
new.tip: Ruins are sparse; a university team still works here, and the views are the draw. Go in dry weather.
new.q: Kerkenes Dağ Arkeolojik Sit Alanı, Şahmuratlı, Sorgun, Yozgat

new.title: See the Çapanoğlu Mosque in Yozgat
new.desc: The Çapanoğlu Mosque, locally the Büyük Camii, was built in 1779 by Çapanoğlu Mustafa Bey, governor of the Bozok sanjak. It is a leading Ottoman baroque monument in the centre of Yozgat.
new.tip: Free; avoid prayer times and dress modestly.
new.q: Çapanoğlu Camii, Yozgat Merkez

new.title: Walk the pine groves of Yozgat Çamlık National Park
new.desc: Declared in 1958, Yozgat Çamlığı is regarded as Turkey's first national park and lies right beside the city centre. It has pine woods, picnic areas, a country restaurant and a viewing terrace.
new.tip: Good for a picnic or barbecue; the park is free and open all year.
new.q: Yozgat Çamlığı Milli Parkı, Yozgat Merkez
